excerpts.author: nordbjerg
excerpts.content:
hey guys, are we supposed to send `["0x", "0x", "0x"]` over engine api if there are no requests? (i.e. empty bytes). or are we supposed to send `[]`, or `["0x0", "0x1", ..]`?

seems like geth posts the first one, but also has this in `core/genesis.go` in `toBlockWithRoot`:

furthermore, if we were to make an `EMPTY_REQUESTS_HASH` constant, would it be the same as sha2(), or would it be `requests_root([0x0, 0x1, 0x2])` or something else? we did the first one, but given below screenshot i'm not sure if we're doing the latter?

excerpts.author: daniellehrner
excerpts.content: ~~I still get a 404 for the link~~ Just now it worked

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content:
for the engine api, it should be `["0x", "0x", "0x"]`

for empty requests hash it is `requests_root([0x0, 0x1, 0x2])`

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: but ^ is not stable across forks like most "empty" hash definitions. if we add a new request type it will need to be updated

excerpts.author: nordbjerg
excerpts.content: wait so when i get 0x 0x 0x over engine api i should interpret it as the requests hash being `requests_root([0x0, 0x1, 0x2])`?

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: yes

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: the data over the engine api has the prefixes removed, whereas the `requests_hash` value includes the prefixes

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: so you need to readd them when computing the block hash

excerpts.author: nordbjerg
excerpts.content: oh wow i see now
